We need to express the summation $S(k+1)$ in terms of $S(k).$

Let ${a}_{i}$ for $i\ge 1$ be a sequence, and let $S(k)$ denote the sum of the first $k$ terms.

$$
S(k)={\sum }_{i=1}^{k}{a}_{i}
$$

We can always express $S(k+1)$ in terms of $S(k)$ by writing the last term on its own, as follows: 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{k+1}{a}_{i}=({\sum }_{i=1}^{k}{a}_{i})+{a}_{k+1}.
$$

In our case, we have ${a}_{i}=2i(i+1).$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{k+1}=2(k+1)(k+1+1)=2(k+1)(k+2).\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{k+1}2i(i+1)=({\sum }_{i=1}^{k}2i(i+1))+(2(k+1)(k+2)),
$$

which we can write as 

$$
S(k+1)=S(k)+2(k+1)(k+2).
$$
